issues.problem: Visibility (radii>0) comes from gsplat 1.5.3's opacity-aware projection (opacity < 1/255 -> radius 0; extent min(3.33, sqrt(2 ln(o/thr)))), not the official fork's 3-sigma radius with no opacity cull. A Gaussian with sigma < 1/255 counts as visible in the official code (its range decays and it adds densify stats) but not in the plugin.
issues.fix: List this explicitly under fidelity gap 2 (it is covered only by the generic 'gsplat rasterizer' line). It applies to every method on the runtime, so the gsplat comparator is unaffected.

issues.problem: The voxel index floor(p/size), with the grid anchored at the origin, is assumed to match Open3D-ML VoxelPooling. ml3d is not installed, so this was not checked against the library. A grid offset would change which Gaussians share a voxel, but not the statistics.
issues.fix: Note it as an unverified assumption in report.md.

issues.problem: The official README example uses --ms_train_max_scale 6, while train_all.py (and the plugin) use 7 for Mip-NeRF 360. 7 agrees with 128x being reported in supp. Tab. 360_per_scene, but the report does not mention that the two sources disagree.

Every non-1x step copies the 1600-px target to the CPU and runs an antialiased bicubic resize there (about 25% of steps). Fidelity is fine (53-84 dB from PIL), but it costs wall-clock time, so the timing is not comparable to the paper's.
issues.fix: Optional: cache the resized targets per (frame, level). Leave it as is if the timing is not reported.

issues.problem: Densification statistics: the official code counts visibility for non-1x renders in per-level accumulators and updates max_radii2D at every level. The plugin accumulates on 1x steps only. Both are inert: only slot 0 is read, and the 20-px screen-size prune never fires because max_radii2D is zeroed before it is read. This is correct, but the report does not say why.
issues.fix: Optional: add one sentence to report.md.

Views are sampled with replacement inside the official per-epoch resolution sequence.

summary: Faithful port of MS-GS @50e5040 and the rasterizer @e7a2b4f. (1) Protocol: train_all.py uses 360_v2 'images' full res, -r -1, so width 1600; max_scale 7; the active 'ms' configuration has test scales 2^0..2^7; training_report evaluates test cameras with the same filter_small/filter_large selection. The dataset's test images are byte-identical to PIL Image.resize(int(W/(g*s)), int(H/(g*s))) of the full-res JPEG (checked garden and counter at 1/4/64x, max diff 0); the 1x train frames are also identical. Split: llffhold 8 on name-sorted frames (garden 161/24). The world frame is not reoriented, so the one-sided contraction acts on the same axes as in the official code. Targets were transcribed correctly from supp. Tab. 360_per_scene (garden 27.16/23.99/26.41/24.79, counter 29.17/26.77/23.44/24.59; 3DGS rows 27.27/20.42/16.74/14.92 and 29.15/24.81/17.94/14.32), and the per-scene means reproduce the main Tab. 1 average (27.39). (2) C1-C4 match the official code line by line: ranges are per Gaussian and updated only for visible Gaussians whose level equals the rendered level (training steps >=250 and >250 after a reset, plus the refresh after insertion); the eval renderer applies the same selection. The sampler, the x0.1 loss, level-0-only ADC/reset/prune and the 30k-then-hold position LR were all confirmed, and the runtime's means-LR override is undone in after_backward. (3) Smoke numbers re-derived from evidence test.json: ms-gs 21.98/21.66/21.11/23.06 and gsplat 22.97/20.62/16.26/14.51. 8 unit tests pass and ss-verify (GPU 6) passes all probes. No critical or major issues; 5 minor issues. Ready for benchmark.
